summary: Greg Alder's Yard Post (Oct 19, 2018) argues that vegetables and melons can be grown under fruit trees to save space, water, time and work, provided the planter matches water and light needs and considers walking paths and mulch. He shares his own successes (watermelon under a Hellen avocado, honeydew under avocado, potatoes in mulch, permanent cilantro patches) and failures (garlic under a nectaplum, overcrowding under a Valencia orange). The post's comment section adds reader experiences and cautions, including verticillium wilt risk and eucalyptus or bottlebrush root and allelopathy concerns.
one_line: Greg Alder's guide to growing melons, potatoes, cilantro and other vegetables under fruit trees in Southern California, matching water and light needs.
key_facts: Greg Alder planted a Sweet Crimson watermelon under a young Hellen avocado tree on June 27, and the partnership worked because both needed lots of water through the summer heat.
The mini-sprinkler on the avocado tree also irrigated the watermelon after the first week or two of hand watering.
Greg Alder grew honeydew melons under another avocado tree, which did great, and called melons and avocado trees an excellent combination.
Garlic planted under his SpiceZee nectaplum tree did not work well because rains never came after the tree lost its leaves, and in spring he ended up with tiny garlic heads.
Greg Alder said garlic would have done better under a citrus tree because citrus trees still need watering through winter if there is no rain.
The garlic must be planted under the south side of a citrus tree, since the north side will be shaded most or all of the day in winter.
Greg Alder put a grape cutting under the north side of a Fuji apple tree, where it grew splendidly without further attention.
Greg Alder planted only a couple of strawberries under the south side of a Pink Lady apple tree so people can walk around the tree to harvest fruit.
Potatoes are one of Greg Alder's favorite vegetables to put under fruit trees because they grow surrounded by mulch and form clean tubers within it.
Greg Alder no longer sows cilantro in vegetable beds; he keeps permanent cilantro patches under fruit trees that self-sow and regrow with the first fall rains.

Greg Alder's Valencia orange tree canopy edge grew peas, tomatoes, beets, bananas, coffee, raspberries, pumpkins, avocado seedlings, potatoes, onions and apricot seedlings in one summer, which was too crowded.
Under the overcrowded Valencia orange tree, light was not sufficient for everything and keeping enough water in the soil during summer heat required extra hand watering.
Wild currants and blackberries grow under the eastern canopy edge of coast live oak trees in Santa Ysabel Preserve, which Greg Alder photographed a couple years earlier.
In a reader comment, Heath noted that UC recommends against planting potatoes and tomatoes near avocados because they can transmit verticillium wilt to avocados.
In a reply, Greg Alder said he once grew vegetables under a eucalyptus tree whose roots constantly and aggressively invaded the vegetable root zones.
